Auditor note

On 2026-11-14 14:03:13 UTC, HostCrust Patch Proof 1.0.0 checked the 16 installed packages of host "Debian 12 synthetic test inventory" (Debian GNU/Linux 12 (bookworm)) against Debian security data published through OSV.dev (snapshot 2026-11-14T11:02:45Z). Packages were matched by source package name and versions were compared with dpkg version rules; the running kernel (6.1.112-1) was checked against the kernel source package 'linux'. The input inventory has SHA-256 dc5a309e70ce324c2e8b584ca7d7010fc8d317c25d8447c0850a9baae9d28bdb; the same input and data snapshot reproduce this report. Result: 69 vulnerabilities have a published fix that is not installed; 5,657 are fixed in an installed kernel that is not running yet; 2,099 have no distro fix yet; 8,177 are fixed, 38 of them by distro backports that version-string scanners commonly misreport. Limits: only distro packages were assessed; 2 package groups built outside the distro were listed but not assessed; containers, language packages, configuration and live kernel patching are out of scope; results are only as current as the data snapshot, and the distro's data decides what counts as affected and fixed.

How this was checked

  • Input: the HostCrust collector (read-only; package and OS metadata only). No hostname or IP address is collected.
  • Data: OSV.dev Debian data, snapshot 2026-11-14T11:02:45Z; bulk file SHA-256 26eb8c0ec8e750d63065dcff324573d348cf5753bb85023dc103fba4e06d7d5e.
  • Matching: source package names (Debian/Ubuntu data is keyed by source package); versions compared with a tested implementation of dpkg ordering.
  • Fixed by backport: the installed version is at or above the distro's fixed version, the data shows an older distro build of the same upstream version (so the fix was a distro patch, not a new upstream release), and the server runs that same upstream version.
  • Severity: the distro's own rating and the CVSS v3 base score from the data, where present. Nothing is rated by this tool.
  • Kernel: kernel vulnerabilities are checked against the running kernel; packages built from the kernel source (headers, tools) are not reported separately.
